But if you're looking for something more interactive than a book, this game might just be for you!
The MC is great, I think she was the high part of the game for me. I like how she is strong and capable, but clearly flawed

It's a rather good VN that managed to simultaneously bore me out, and surprise me a few times)
How can that be? Well, the plot is utterly predictable, and the characters are utterly dense, but some details still come as a surprise

In short: good graphics, nice music, rather 3d characters, a goofy story with 'high stakes' and basic logic present, and endless tedious melodrama from the FL

Now, regarding routes. It is a CRIME that Callum's route is blocked during the first playthrough. I was aiming for it on purpose and ended up left without allies at all. And that's a tad frustrating, so keep in mind that you should go through someone else's route first.

[b]Nazagi[/b] is your regular dangerous manipulator, but with basic morals)
In his bad ending, [spoiler]you'll end up with a wiped memory on your way home.[/spoiler]
So the writer gave him an 'ends justify means' attitude without making him ruthless.
His good ending is a surprise on its own. [spoiler]God knows power trouple was not something I expected)[/spoiler]

Actually, I enjoyed this route the most. Probably, because there's at least a semblance of intrigues going on, and constant 'tension'.

[b]Oscar[/b] is a pvetty honeypie with love for poetry and pouting (his route literally depends on his feelings). Well, considering the FL's love for whining in her thoughts they might be a good match after all. His route is the main one as I understand, so it contains the most variability in regards to details (got to replay it many times to find all small differences).

Overall it's a farytale-like story that made me consider dropping the game overall. If you're not into melodrama better to try something else on your first playthrough. Because I literally have nothing interesting to say about this one 0-0

[b]Gaston's[/b] route is my second favorite one. If you think you figured that guy out, no you didn't) Just wait until the ending, you'll be surprised)
Unexpectedly his route is the most funny, and wholesome one ever. Love it!

The funny thing is as this character is mild-hearted, mind that the ending depends on how compassionate you prove yourself to be. One shallow observation may cost you quite a lot (wink)

And I think that this route is probably the best ending overall: I believe that most characters will be happy (truly)

[b]Callum's[/b] your spicy brooding boy, and you hit off with him after one(!) conversation. Even FL acknowledges that it's way too sudden, and swift to say the least.

What you should keep in mind is that despite the missing stakes you can't pull out of the game per se. It's either you end up together, or you'll face consequences. Unless you wish to switch sides (wink)

His route makes the most sense, but I still prefer the Gaston's or Nazagi's over it.  No intrigues going on, apparent danger, or tension until the end. And it totally makes sense: you are under royalty members' protection after all.

His good ending is one of the best for the FL, and I think they suit each other, but I don't appreciate any ending where Cassidy is not together with the gushing blond)

Now regarding switching sides. Depending on the way you treated the [b]page (Dolores)[/b] you may 'free' yourself together with her. Of course that will come at a price of [spoiler]betraying your newfound lover, Cassidy, Oscar, possibly ruining country overall, and stealing country's assets once again[/spoiler]

Is it worth it? I'm not sure, especially considering that [spoiler]Dolores will be better off staying as princess's friend in any ending.[/spoiler] But it's a possibility nonetheless that gains this game a plus.

Also, I once again enjoyed how the game punishes you for foolish actions and indecisiveness: [spoiler]if you're willing to throw a state in turmoil, at least be faithful to it, and run away yourself.[/spoiler]
And a cherry on top: if you're willing to lie openly, don't expect to be trusted)

Overall it could be better, but nothing is perfect)
Thanks for a few fun evenings!

I was intrigued by the main character actually seeming powerful and capable, judging by the introductory store page art and initial story presentation, I decided to pick it up during a sale and I was not disappointed at all.

The main character is beautiful, smart, witty and very capable, which is a true gem in a genre dominated by naive, weak and incapable female leads. The other characters also feel well fleshed out and believable, each of them with their own unique personality traits and quirks.
However, character development is pretty much non-existent in almost all cases outside of you actually getting to know the characters as you play.

Endings can be surprising and not what you expect, which can be off-putting to some and a breath of freshness for others. 

The individual storylines are unique and they all add to the overarching storyline, which is great and surprisingly deep. It threw me for a loop and I loved it. Depending on which route you go for the romance goes from sweet to steamy passionate, so that's a good mix as well. Some of the routes are locked in the beginning of the game and that can feel a bit stale, but as you play you will be able to unlock them fairly easily.

The art style seems hand drawn for the characters and can initially be off-putting to some people, but it isn't bad and truly shines during certain scenes. Some of the backdrops are gorgeous. The music is good as well.

I found myself being quickly drawn in by the story and I wanted more. The game feels a little short, but for what it is I feel the price is fair (15 euros at the time of writing this).

总体来说，感觉这游戏还行，西方人写宫廷阴谋故事有那种西方特有的味道。但是恋爱非常少，大篇幅在讲阴谋，密谋故事还行，但是除了二周目才开的真相线Callum & Dolores线以外，其他线都或多或少保留了一部分真相。搞得一定要通真相线阴谋故事才完整，但论恋爱好多线甚至谈不上有恋爱，有点不上不下。

我是把Callum & Dolores线留到最后通的，但是前几个周目看女主要恋爱没多少恋爱，要剧情又一直在折腾前面已清楚的真相又不给新的情报时会有点着急。一周目就在疑惑Dolores的身份了，结果一直拖到Callum happy end才搞清楚，Oscar线甚至全篇没去探索Dolores身份问题，留个钩子迷惑的结尾感觉不太好。[strike] 但是Oscar的感情线弥补了这一点 [/strike]

我感觉Oscar线算是最像乙游路线的一条了，至少真有谈恋爱，Callum也还算恋爱，其他人感觉完全是合作伙伴队友的关系。

女主还不错的，有主见有想法，是真有在为自己的将来打算，挺理智的，不是挂件，但也没厉害到能装个逼的程度，主线更像悬疑探秘，所以我才抱怨有的线路探秘没揭露秘密体验不好了。

整体因为女主身份比较低，而且是三王子追求公主的背景，偶尔有真实但略憋屈的感觉，行动处处受限，不太舒服。

音乐一般，有的还行，有的我觉得太过嘈杂，但还过得去。

画风非常有特色，但是个人感觉谈不上好看。同样厚涂风格《海市蜃楼之馆》就美型很多，但是也不能把小型作品该作与海馆比。

伏笔不错，谜面还行，但反转谈不上优秀，略有点那种靠机械将神反转的感觉。反转确实意料之外情理之中，但有点太硬，比较依赖一个非常不同寻常的真相做反转，撂推理作品里我会对谜底失望的那种水平，那种不在场证明思考了半天结果谜底双胞胎，密室研究了半天结果有密道，情理之中，但不够精彩。

总体而言感觉还行，打折可以入，但是专门为了恋爱来不行，为了阴谋来凑合，为了西方宫廷来可以，宫廷部分挺有特色的，宫廷密谋的氛围和人物身份背景比较地道，毕竟西方作品写西方故事，会少很多外国人视角的粉饰和童话妄想情怀，有点意思。

I actually enjoyed this game quite a bit. I bought it a very long time ago but never played it. It has a lot more action and intrigue than many of the visual novels that I have read, and it was a welcome break from the standard romance centered novel. I did have one very big problem though. The entire mystery concerning Cassidy is VERY problematic. On one hand it is a great plot device and adds a unique spin on the game. On the other hand the implication of said mystery presents quite a few disturbing complications that are either completely glossed over or not even discussed at all. The ramifications of these complications are handled with equal superficiality. Apparently the writer doesn't seem to think that there are larger issues to be discussed because a happy ending is a happy ending, end of story. We're talking about real deception playing out on a grand scale, and it isn't even properly addressed. Despite my enjoyment of the game, it does present some larger issues that should have been explored. The end result of some of these could even have played into a great potentially BAD ending.

英文全通尽量无剧透的评测如下：
世界观的继承法理是反向萨利克，女有男无，女主Madeleine是穷困小贵族的次女，机缘巧合帮了闯祸的小王子Oscar一把被国王任命为王子贴身侍女，王子长大成人即将结婚，女主也开始为自己卸任之后的职业前途考虑，故事从参加邻国公主Cassidy的成年礼开始
虽然人物设定表面看很日系乙女套路，事实上剧情悬疑成分重，有多次反转，加上另外一些要素让我认为这个游戏其实与其说是乙女不如说是带有恋爱要素的悬疑视觉小说，人物塑造优秀，文笔不错，音乐好听，CG不抱什么期待的话还有点小惊喜（？）
流程不长，英语阅读熟练者大概5-6个小时可以不跳过全通，总体来讲是一个让我屡屡感叹“2015年的洋妞居然能如此放飞”“啊这设定好白左不过居然写得可以”的游戏，不愧是女王万岁制作组怎么说
1. Oscar，青梅竹马阳光少年，开场好感基本拉满，正统乙女剧情没啥好说的，大概也是这种王道系路线的角色通病就是没有很明确的记忆点，这条线相比之下我对Duke Pherod的印象更深一点
2. Nazagi，神秘冷淡美人，由于个人能力过于牛逼这条线女主在解谜方面并没有发挥多少作用只管等着他给结论就是了，主要是敲他的冰壳子，HE结局是让我感慨洋妞可以这么放飞的吗的第一个点，但很合理，显然不是作者放飞XP一拍脑袋而是慎重考虑过人设和剧情导向的结果：政治婚姻和爱情是不挂钩的（说实话有些小妹妹在一个剧情大背景就是准备政治联姻的游戏里要求什么这不行那不行的真的没毛病吗建议有病吃药
3. Gaston，过分热情的花花公子，第一眼觉得有点油，在后半的某个情节里只用一句话一个动作就反转刻板印象好感度拉满了，这条线也是我认为这游戏不应该视为乙女游戏的原因之一，具体原因剧透不谈，另外这条线开始对Cassidy有了比较深入的描写所以在Callum之前推掉会比较好

So I usually prefer novels with a stronger more headfast female lead and this VN does have that, and it is the reason I bought it in the first place. The VN however, is undoubtedly short af and I wonder if it's worth the price point. But, nevertheless  I enjoyed it mildly (please notice the modern english to traditional english here) which if you really can't handle it then do not buy the VN at all. Mild fascinating plot twists and the catchy music were the only interesting points. 

Madeleine Valois is a valet of a the prince of Oceandwyr and is on a mission to help the prince secure a bride. However, the prince has someone already in his mind and is not willing to let go of her. What will Maddie do? Is it the duty or the heart that comes first? Meanwhile, they arrive at a new kingdom and gets tangled in a weird plot of dark royal family affairs and betrayals. Have a peek at this utterly medieval theme based VN with princes with an unusual story line to find out. 

Cute lil summary: 

PROS: Music 100, Gender Bender 1000, Strong female lead 100, Weird Dark Story 100, Gaston as a prince 100 
CONS: Short routes, aged old formal English, unfair price  

[b] Story [/b]
The story is emotional and sentimental at first, the girl is like a bodyguard and the prince is in love with her. It is sort of a forbidden love story where the ends cannot meet, and the prince have to marry someone else. The MC has no royalty whatsoever but a weak noble. but that itself is interesting. The story is pretty much rational and logical, displaying intelligence of the main protagonist. Other than that, everything is kind of boring, the looong descriptions of kingdoms and their relationships will bore the reader out if you are not into this sort of a thing. Also the story lacks depth and seems very rushed with the routes. There are 5 routes together and 4 of them are princes and the last being a servant girl. My personal opinion is that the princess's route should have been included if an irrelevant servant girl is added lol which would have been the most epic story line in a straight otome VN. The story has elements of dark backstories, assassinations, forced gender transition, neglect, unpredictable friendships and some slight erotica. I do feel like the darker aspects of the routes are not executed a bit dramatically so you don't feel the pain of the characters. The questions about the mysterious gender transition are only fully answered if you finish every route. 

[b] Characters [/b] 
Set of interesting, a bit contrasting characters. The MC herself is very strong, armed in combat and is intellectual. The prince she serves, seems timid, soft hearted, loyal yet displays interesting opposite traits. The princess's brother seems aloof, neglected, lonely and family oriented. The beauty and the beast prince tho, LITERALLY inspired from that character Gaston(?) and got on my nerves immediately but he still had some surprising traits. Lastly, the ice prince. He is a farmakeist and dark one at that, seems manipulative and has a princess and the frog backstory. 
Seems like the authors, took some elements of other fairy tales but was just thrown randomly in the story which is disappointing. Dolores is the one I disliked the most for obvious reasons. She is just in for the dimes. For some of the characters there are slight progressions in their character development but nothing major, the princess on the other hand is the most attractive (I'm not gay or bi, but then she has a dark secret which makes you think so) She is literally the most interesting character of the whole story with some character development at least. Her parents and relatives seem to be very cold but one can ponder when you are at the highest peaks of power, is it ethical that someone would utilize greed and political manipulation using their own family as bait to ensure their success? I shall never know (oops went formal just like the VN) 

[b] Gameplay[/b] 
The game difficulty is very easy, idk why should there be an effort to even think. The settings have an auto play button, a skip button and all the necessities. I did like at first that the dialogue box where the text is displayed is on the right which is not something you see every day, but the box is with great height and a lot of text is being displayed which makes my mind not want to read it for some reason. Initially the text display speed is way too fast for me, very fast so I had to adjust that. Also this VN is mighty SHORT, the character routes are over before you know it. Another thing is, the whole story is narrated in very formal English with some sprinkles of French, which makes me wonder if all characters are French. Minus the French it can bore you or sometimes it feels like you are reading aged Shakespeare poetry and you will fall asleep in 10 seconds. 

[b] Art and Music [/b] 
The art of the sprites are pretty much okay, but I did not like the CG art of the characters. This has been a flaw of many visual novels I have read, always the sprite art has to be different of the CG character art. The landscape shots are also okay. The music is what takes the cake in this whole VN, interesting music! It feels latin/mexican vibes and I am all for that. Those pieces were very much atmospheric and I greatly appreciate it. 

[b] Achievements [/b] 
Achievements are not hard to get and for each ending (Good, Normal, Bad) you get an achievement unlocked for each character.  The normal endings I found, are a bit harder to get than the good or bad ones but not super difficult at all. 

[b] Overall [/b]
A very short medieval western VN which had a great potential to be an interesting story but got ruined by rushed routes, no or very little character development yet I am going to recommend it because I saw some elements which I haven't seen in other VN's. Found myself that I needed unusual motivation and I procrastinated a lot to finish this. Its very recommended to buy it during sale because I have played much better and lengthy VN's at a less price.

Some minimally spoilery thoughts below.

I enjoyed the story a lot, lots of intrigue and surprising developments. Most LIs were interesting to me as well, though some of them certainly had more room in the story than others. What I'm most conflicted about is the representation of queerness in the story. On certain routes it is very central to the story, but at the same time both in regards to the game mechanics and within the story itself queerness is something to be tucked away, to be kept secret or at least private. So YMMV on how you feel about this. In some ways it is very realistic (to real life as well), but not necessarily what you want if you prefer out, loud and proud in a world that supports that.

I imagine that partially it shows as well that this game came out in 2015 and things have already changed a lot since.

There's also a very complex situation in which self-determination/self-identification and bodily autonomy are supported and undermined at the same time, that's quite a doozy.

So, there's some heavy themes as you uncover the secrets of why things are as they are. There are plenty of lighter moments, as well, and I would by no means consider this a dark story. The bad ends may end with your death, but the happy ends are rather sweet.

For the story structure, you have a few common chapters at the start followed by route-specific chapters (for the most part, each LI has their own route). You have some choices that impact how the story unfolds, but mostly your choices make a difference on which route you land on and which ending you get. There's some variation within the chapters / routes based on what you choose, but no huge branching plotlines.

TL;DR: Interesting story with mystery and court intrigue, butterflies and drama, interesting and distinct LIs and routes. YMMV on how you feel about the queer aspects, but they're definitely there and important, even if the handling and presenting of them is rather complex.

If you like strong heroines, The Confines of the Crown is the game for you. Madeleine is cunning, a good fighter, and has a high amount of agency. She's often the first to react in dire situations, whether that's disarming an enemy or planning the next step in solving the mysteries. Some might consider her TOO perfect. but I think she strikes the right balance of badass but not overpowered.

The love interests are good too, though some characters were clearly given more care than others (Oscar, Callum). The other routes are low on the romance, but the plot still held my interest. I do wish there were more romantic scenes, but the game takes place over a very short period of time, so it's understandable considering that.

The one character that disappointed me was [spoiler]Gaston[/spoiler] for two reasons. I don't mind that he is not a romantic interest, but naming the route after him and featuring him in the OP gave me the impression he would be. Secondly, while the way he fetishizes lesbian relationships is perhaps realistic to how some heterosexual men act, I did not find it charming or humorous. The game presents it as harmless fun, but if you are sensitive to negative portrayals of LGBTQ themes, I would proceed with caution. That said, the game is nearly 7 years old and handles other LGBTQ scenes with more grace, so it's a mixed bag rather than a huge negative.

The art is beautiful. There are plenty of CGs and the sprites are also well-done. Cassidy is so pretty; truly looks like a princess! They were truly a treat to look at while I played.

Again, no complaints with the soundtrack. The songs were catchy, suited the mood, and not overplayed to the point of being tiresome.

The writing is The Confines of the Crown's biggest strength. The language is appropriately formal and detailed and the characterization is consistent. It's impressive how the mysteries are weaved throughout the different routes, giving you only small snippets of the truth each time. The truth was not predictable, nor did it come out of nowhere, so it left me satisfied.

I do wish the game was a bit longer, but the writing was so tight that I prefer it this way to being dragged out past its welcome. Overall, I had a very positive experience with this game and would recommend it to anyone who enjoys visual novels or mysteries.

Hanako Games' finest work! The Confines of the Crown, or, The Royal Trap, as it was initially called, is a clever and well-written story involving royal intrigue, scandals and cover-ups, and betrayal.

It also involves their best artwork to date. The sprites need a little work, but the CGs are phenomenally beautiful. I kept marveling and posting screenshots because the art style is so unique, and incredibly gorgeous. It's like a blend of anime and Western style animation, with a heavy, painted style. The colors are vibrant and bring out the emotions of the scene well. 

The story is written tightly and with a certain eloquent charm one might expect in an actual novel about royal families. It can get lengthy at times, but none of it is tedious to read, in my opinion. The narrative style is lively and engaging, and Maddie's internal monologues add to the depth of the story and your empathy with her and her life.

The music is varied and fun, from lively guitars to James Bond-esque music for when the heroine is stealthing around and doing her job as the valette of a prince -- gathering info to aid him and his pursuits.

The characters are all fun and/or fascinating, and each route is wonderful because it's not just a rehash of prior events with some new romance -- it reveals a different chunk of the mystery at the heart of things. By the time you've finished each route, you have the whole picture of what's been happening in the royal family of Gwellinor.

The guys are all very interesting and gorgeous. There's the sadistic Nazagi, whose endings are quite thrilling/salacious, the blustering macho-man Gaston (still on his route), the non-heir (and thus disregarded and outcast) prince of Gwellinor Callum, and of course, your prince Oscar, the boy you've been serving since you were children.

All the routes are entertaining and enjoyable, even though I love some more than others. I highly recommend this for a good read and some sweet romance.

P.S. Lambert the Guard is the best [apart from Callum].

The Confines Of The Crown is one of the visual novels that I enjoyed the most. The protagonist is a really strong factor when it comes to liking or not this kind of games and in this case Madeleine Valois is a constituted character that stands by itself and is not only charismatic but keeps you on every route grateful in some way of being so great, because you'll have to face many dangerous and delicate situations that we'll wouldn't otherwise be able to solve. All the characters are equally interesting and well developed, each route is different and the connection that Madeleine has with them goes according to their personalities, it doesn't feel forced, which I appreciate because it gives an extra original touch to a story that is already very original and complex but that closes perfectly even being a fantasy story. Without a doubt, there is a lot of versatility and even the secondary characters bring humor and sustain the story throughout the game along with the main characters. I appreciate that there's the possibility of having a romantic relationship with women and men, as well as in another routes and endings you'll be able to choose something else for personal reasons (I don't want to spoil anything because it's really worth playing it, many things in this game are not what they seem). Also, although it may not be touched in depth, the questioning of one's gender is approached a bit (of course within the context of a game and in the middle of a fantasy story context), something that could have been offensive but is not and fits within the narrative of the game, I think that's positive as well. What begins as a political conflict soon develops into something much bigger and we can appreciate from the point of view of Madeleine Valois how her life was and how she came to be where she is, and more importantly, where she would like to be and her dreams, in that way we have to accompany her and based on our choices we can have many different endings. Unfortunately, plots are afoot that complicate their visit, and as Madeleine it is the player's job to navigate the resulting political intrigue successfully in a fashion that benefits both herself and her childhood friend and employer, Prince Oscar. 

There are 5 routes -"Alliances"- that Madeleine can make, & each has multiple endings. To get the "good endings" you'll need to secure the best position for yourself and make sure Oscar makes it out ok. I really liked this concept. Madeleine is resourceful, sharp, fierce, and far from passive, which was a very refreshing change from many visual novel heroines. Although I feel I should point out that if you are looking for a romantic visual novel, you'd be better off choosing a different game. Of the 5 possible routes, only 2 of them have romantic interests/subplots. The focus of this novel is primarily on the mysteries and the political drama.

This game came as a big surprise as it did not meet my purchase criteria:  I thought I was buying an otome VN, and sure enough there is a little smattering of romance to be found here and there within.  However, that really is only a very small part of the whole.  What I got was an incredibly well crafted, deep mystery of political intrigue that had me utterly hooked in spite of my expectations.

There are four “main” routes to follow, plus a very short fifth one which can only be found from within one of the other four; each one supplying additional story detail that you will not find anywhere else.  This provides a decent amount of replayability, and with judicious use of the skip function, you should be able to play through all routes and all options without ever becoming bored with any repetition.

I've seen it said that there are ugly character graphics, and also that the art is beautiful.  Both of these statements are true.  The king is ugly, whether by accident or design, I don't know.  The MC sprite is beautifully drawn, and so are some of the CG scenes she appears in – notably the good end of two routes and when at the lake; and yet at some other times she looks angular, masculine and bare of detail, like she had been idly doodled during a tea break.

All characters you meet have some level of depth and while this varies from one to another, none of them are paper-thin nor uninteresting; and most of them bear a surprise or two waiting to be discovered.

Your options come at irregular intervals and I would challenge any assertion you may have already seen which claims that many of them make no difference.  On some occasions I found the response to my choice was affected by something I had said or done previously in addition to what I had just chosen.  For this reason, I recommend saving often, especially after you clear chapter 4.  There are certainly [i]loads[/i] of save spots available, and if it helps, you can name them too (although this is not compulsory.  Leave them blank and the date and time goes in instead.)

Overall, if you are after a dating-sim, then this is not the right choice for you; but if you like a good, deep story which will have you thoroughly engaged; or a mystery that you like to see unravelled gradually; then – irrespective of your gender - this is an excellent purchase to make and a very worthy addition to your visual novel collection.

É um jogo interessante com uma história não tão óbvia. É uma boa visual novel, mas não se tornou uma das minhas favoritas. Os personagens são interessantes, mas as interações não foram o suficiente pra eu me apegar a eles, muito menos causar grandes emoções nas rotas, com exceção de uma e talvez outra. Segue um resumo:

[b]Romance:[/b] é leve, em 3 das 5 rotas você sequer tem certeza se há algum sentimento além do de cumplicidade e talvez atração física. Mas gostei também que dependendo da rota há uma atenção maior para o valor de uma amizade.

[b]Enredo:[/b] Achei interessante, em algumas rotas há mais intrigas que em outras, mas no geral sem grandes emoções ou conteúdo muito maduro. É interessante pra passar o tempo e fácil de ler, mas eu diria que é o tipo de história que você não ficará pensando sobre após terminar o jogo, é fácil de esquecer e seguir sua vida, diferentemente de algumas VNs que realmente deixam aquela sensação de "vazio" ao acabarem de tão boas. [spoiler]Eu gostei que eles abordaram um tema bem único: transgêneros/transexuais. Nunca vi esse tema em um jogo desses antes. Gostei da forma que escreveram sobre isso também, achei respeitosa e neutra.[/spoiler]

[b]A personagem principal:[/b] eu adorei a personalidade dela. Ela é forte, astuta, manipuladora, ágil, sabe lutar, decidida e corajosa. Como uma grande fã de visual novel e jogos otome, eu gostaria de ver mais personagens assim, geralmente somos obrigados a aturar mulheres agindo como meninas de 8 anos puras, ingênuas e inofensivas.

[b]Rotas e personagens:[/b] A rota que mais me causou emoções de nervosismo, ansiedade, tristeza, felicidade e etc [spoiler]e também a mais romântica[/spoiler] foi a do Oscar. O personagem que a personalidade mais me agradou e interessou foi o Nazagi, porém achei que faltou explorarem mais, ele tinha um grande potencial e a personalidade mais complexa e misteriosa de todas. A rota do Callum é inicialmente bloqueada e é a minha segunda favorita, pois foi a segunda que mais me apeguei ao personagem, [spoiler]especialmente por ter um pouco mais de romance que o Gaston ou o Nazagi ou a Dolores, mas também por ele ter um passado e presente tristes. A rota do Callum junto com a do Nazagi são as que mais dão informações sobre o que de fato está acontecendo no reino, então foram interessantes pra entender as motivações de cada um.[/spoiler] A rota do Gaston não me interessou nenhum pouco, achei muito forçada e teatral, mas isso é muito pessoal. A da Dolores também é pouco explorada, mas gosto da personalidade dela.

[b]Nota geral:[/b] 8/10 [spoiler]pelas rotas do Oscar e do Callum, se não a nota seria 7 por achar que os outros personagens foram tratados de forma muito superficial.[/spoiler]

Auch wenn [i]The Confines of the Crown[/i] als Otome gelistet ist, ist es kein typisches Otome Spiel. Ich würde es eher als Visual Novel einstufen, denn hier geht es vor allem um die Geschichte, die eine Vielzahl von Charakteren, Beziehungen und Enden bereithällt. Diese beinhalten, bis auf zwei Außnahmen, auch nicht immer eine romantische Beziehung bzw. ein typisches Otome-Happy-End. Aber genau das ist es was mir an diesem Spiel so gut gefällt. 

Wegen der kurzen Spieldauer empfehle ich aber auf einen Sale zu warten. Dort wird es für 4,99€ angeboten und zu diesem Preis habe ich das Spiel auch gekauft.

[h1]Kurz zur Handlung[/h1]
Die Geschichte beginnt damit wie wir, alias Madeleine Valois, Prinz Oscar von Oceandawyr auf den Ball von Prinzessin Cassidy von Gwellinor vorbereiten. In der Hoffnung ihr Herz gewinnen zu können, denn in dieser Welt ist es so, dass die erstgeborene Tochter den Familientitel weitergibt und das Vermögen erbt, während die Söhne in der Pflicht sind sich möglichst gut zu vermählen. Diese sind dann zwar offiziell als Könige die Herrscher aber die Königinnen, die als [i]Weisheiten[/i] betitelt werden, haben die eigentliche Macht und dienen als offizielle Berater. 

Um sicherzustellen das alles beim Ball bestens verläuft, begleiten wir den Prinzen dorthin. Natürlich bleibt es nicht lange ruhig und wir befinden uns inmitten der politischen Fehden, die all unser Können, unsere Loyalität und Freundschaft zu Oscar auf die Probe stellen. Können wir unseren Prinzen beschützen? Und zu welchen Preis? Und welches Geheimnis versteckt Prinzessin Cassidy?

[h1]Gameplay & Charaktere[/h1]
Leider gibt es durch die sehr kurze Spieldauer, nicht genug Raum um der Geschichte und allen Charakteren gerecht zuwerden. Während man Madeleine und Prinzessin Cassidy wirklich gut kennen lernt, erfährt man über die meisten anderen Hauptcharaktere fast gar nichts. Das bedeutet aber nicht, dass die Charaketere nicht interessant wären.  Im Gegenteil, auch wenn das Spiel viele Otome Klischees bedient, haben alle noch ein gewisses Etwas, was sie irgentwie doch von der Masse abhebt.

Die Hauptgeschichte selbst hat mich von Anfang bis Ende gefesselt. Dadurch, dass jede der Routen ein separates Stück der Geschichte erzählt, gibt es einen großen Wiederspielwert. Dank ein paar unerwartenden Wendungen hat man immer wieder AHA-Momente bis sich zum Schluss alle Teile zusammenfügen. 
Es gibt eine angenehme Anzahl an Entscheidungen zu treffen, deren Ausgang aber leider etwas zu sehr vorhersehbar ist. 

Ich bin froh, dass dieses Spiel sich an einige schwierigen Themen wie Transsexualität, Intersexualität und Homosexualität heranwagt und meiner Meinung nach auch respektvoll behandelt. 
Auch sehr erfrischend ist, dass unsere "Heldin" zur Abwechslung mal gut auf sich alleine aufpassen kann. Madeleine ist intelligent, unabhängig und stark und das alles ohne auch nur ein Stück von ihrer Weiblichkeit einzubüßen. 

[h1]Musik & Grafik[/h1]
Die Musik ist ganz ok. Der Soundtrack ist nicht allzu umfangreich und wiederholt sich sehr oft. Die CGs und Hintergründe sind größtensteils wirklich sehr schön aber die Sprites sind von der Qualität ein großes Durcheinander.
Besonders gut hat mir gefallen, dass größere Textabschnitte in einem extra Kasten angezeigt wurden und man nicht alles einfach in das kleine Dialogfeld gepackt hat.

-极其糟糕的自由度
这款游戏可以分为以下几条线
A 没有任何盟友的坏结局(故事只能看到第四章，就会强制进入结局)
B Oscar线

D Gaston线

其中EF两条线是较早能抓住真相尾巴的，但是它们在第一轮被禁掉了！！！更可气的是A线是不计入通关次数的，想玩到EF线，必须得先通掉BCD中的任意一个。
而且不像别人说的，知道真相，玩到chapter3就差不多了……

-谜之选项判定
第一次无法攻略Callum/Dolores是因为有一个选项被锁定了，封掉一个选项，Callum和Dolores两条线就废了。所以应该有很多选项都是对结局判定没啥用的。

最差的A线结局，开局15分钟的选项就能达成，后面几个小时简直在浪费时间啊，因为开局就注定了结局，后面怎么选都没用的。

-剧本没有内核
这个剧本反转很多次，很容易读完。在疲劳的时候就会来个转折，节奏很不错。但就像缺了主旨立意的文章，看完就是哈哈一乐，很多时候只是单纯的为了反转而反转，而且有些反转就是为了猎奇。仿佛本子写作者先画了一条时间轴，然后在上面点了几个点，提醒自己这里要反转，然后填进去了点什么。不过考虑到这毕竟只是个小厂AVG，能做到让大家轻松愉快的读完也可以了...
游戏里的人物塑造的挺不错的，女主真的很优秀！

-音乐
非常好听，虽然我觉得有些场景的气氛跟配乐根本合不起来，但是每个人对音乐气氛的感受都不一样，所以这只是我的感觉。不过音乐真的很好听。

综上所述，这可以是一个不错的游戏，思路是好的，剧本核心要是再好点就好了。强行控制自由度真的非常讨厌，既然是我玩游戏，我应该有权利决定我想怎么玩，花多久去玩。生活本来就如此不易，玩个AVG还不能追自己喜欢的人物，简直丧心病狂。

The Royal Trap: The Confines of the Crown is a visual novel by Hanako Games, made "famous" some time ago for Long Live the Queen and a plethora of other minor sims. Although it appears to be an otome game from the premise, I found that it was much less of an otome and more of a short story about petty misunderstandings and your token ""strong female protagonist"" (double quotes) with a sprinkle of gender equality.
As far as gameplay goes, its your standard Ren'Py visual novel with copy-paste menu screens and buttons with the added benefit of storing walls of text on one side of the screen instead of full page.

The reader is put into the shoes of Madeleine Valois, a noblewoman who's been appointed as personal guardian, spy and agent of a prince in a fantasy land; she will be following him from their own kingdom to another, in the hopes that her master will meet and marry a beautiful princess, next heir to the throne. As it is customary in this type of fiction, a conspiracy ensues, with political intrigue, assassinations, deception and mystery.... or so you'd think. And romance? What about romance? Technically there is, but its limited to two routes, which are far from being a shining example of good narrative.
Madeleine is constantly boosted as a girl with "equipment and special gloves that let her climb walls, daggers etc." someone who is supposed to be a highly trained combatant, well versed in subterfuge; however, as I have already mentioned in other reviews, these kinds of novels are very deceptive as they deliberately frame their protagonist as strong willed and fierce, but ultimately resort to cheap narrative that destroys their accomplishments and diminishes their value to highlight their fragility.
This novel is no exception, as the ever-resourceful Madeleine can't even escape a simple prison cell. She is also easily confined in her quarters and very submissive to total strangers, letting blunt and careless men steal kisses like its nothing. That is mildly infuriating, to say the least.
Speaking of "strong female protagonists", there is almost no action whatsoever that might even remotely justify Madeleine's supposed strength, except for one brief moment in the prologue. Every time she is called to perform an action that might require her actual talents, using any of her repertoire results in a bad end - she gets killed immediately.

As for the narrative, a series of convenient misunderstandings clears everyone from suspicion, reducing what could have been an interesting development into smoke and mirrors. The male entourage either has the personality of a rock or simply sit there to make statements about homosexuality and gender equality, which, although completely fair, is not a suitable example of character development. People do not exist in a bubble of ideals.
I did enjoy Gaston's Happy Ending though, highly recommended as the last route for maximum payoff. That's the canon ending to me.
